config.chat.provider: Provider for the **chat** model. `local` = Ollama / LM Studio / llama.cpp on your machine or your server: no data leaves the network.
config.completion.provider: Provider for **inline completion**. Keep it `local`: this is the number-one cost driver elsewhere (one request per keystroke pause).
config.completion.debounceMs: Idle time before a completion is requested.
config.endpoints.local: URL of the local OpenAI-compatible server (Ollama: .../v1, LM Studio: http://127.0.0.1:1234/v1, vLLM, llama.cpp…).
config.endpoints.openaiCompatible: URL of an internal OpenAI-compatible gateway (corporate proxy, Azure, LiteLLM…).
config.privacy.redaction:
Pseudonymisation before any **remote** request:
- `strict`: credentials, identities, machines, paths, internal URLs, IP addresses — reversibly replaced.
- `balanced`: credentials and identities only.
- `off`: none (discouraged, and it requires `privacy.allowUnredacted`).
config.privacy.allowUnredacted: Actually honour the “off” level. Without this box ticked, “off” falls back to “balanced”.
config.privacy.blockedGlobs: Files that NEVER reach a remote provider, whatever else is configured.
config.privacy.egressPolicy: Confirm before the first remote request of a session (ask-once), before every request (ask-always), or never (trust).
config.privacy.auditLog: Log every remote request locally (timestamp, provider, model, tokens, cost). Never the content.
config.budget.perRequestUsd: Maximum estimated cost of one remote request. Beyond it, the request is refused.
config.budget.dailyUsd: Daily cap on remote spending. 0 = no cap.
config.context.maxTokens: Token budget for the context sent to the model (repository map + excerpts).
config.context.repoMap: Attach a map of the repository's symbols rather than whole files.
config.privacy.customTerms: Organisation-specific words to always replace before a remote request: client names, project names, internal brands.
config.escalation.policy: When the local model is not enough (context too large, a diagnosis or architecture question): `never` refuses, `ask` offers, `auto` switches to the escalation model on its own.
config.language: Interface language. `auto` follows the editor's display language.

config.mcp.servers: MCP servers to connect to, as `{ "name": { … } }`. A `stdio` entry runs a program on this machine and is never started until you have agreed to it in a dialog that names the command; an `http` entry talks to a URL and goes through the same egress rules as any other outbound request. A `.vscode/mcp.json` in the workspace is read too, and these entries win on a name collision.

config.accounts:
**Accounts.** API keys are never stored in settings — they go to your operating system's keychain, because this file syncs between machines and gets committed by accident.

- [Store a key](command:hiveyCode.setApiKey) for OpenRouter, Anthropic or an OpenAI-compatible gateway
- [Forget a key](command:hiveyCode.clearApiKey)
- [Open the setup screen](command:hiveyCode.setup) to find a local model or connect an account
- [Store the ARCAD Elias credentials](command:hiveyCode.setArcadCredentials)

config.panel.minWidth: Narrowest the panel is allowed to become, in pixels. Below this the panel scrolls sideways instead of rearranging itself, so dragging the side bar narrow cannot reshuffle the layout. `0` lets it shrink freely.
config.permissions.autoApprove:
How much the agent may do without asking.

Whatever this is set to, `#hiveyCode.privacy.blockedGlobs#` still applies and what leaves the machine is still governed by `#hiveyCode.privacy.egressPolicy#`. This setting changes how often you are interrupted — never what the agent is allowed to touch, and never what it may send.
config.permissions.autoApprove.workspace: Changes inside the open folder run without asking. Commands, and anything outside the folder, are still asked for.
config.permissions.autoApprove.all: Nothing is asked. Dangerous: the agent may write anywhere and run anything.
config.permissions.allowedPaths: Paths the agent may change without asking, as globs relative to the workspace root — `src/generated/**`, `docs/*.md`. Applies whatever the approval scope is. Paths matching `#hiveyCode.privacy.blockedGlobs#` are refused even when listed here.
config.permissions.allowedCommands: Commands that may run without asking, matched by prefix on a word boundary: `npm test` allows `npm test -- --watch` and not `npm testpublish`. A command containing `;`, `&&`, `|`, a backtick or `$(` is never covered, however it starts.
config.permissions.deniedPaths:
Paths the agent may never change, as globs — `migrations/**`, `dist/**`. Refusals are evaluated before permissions, so a path here is refused even if `#hiveyCode.permissions.allowedPaths#` lists it and even with approvals switched off.

Distinct from `#hiveyCode.privacy.blockedGlobs#`, which is about what may LEAVE the machine. This is about what may be touched on it.
config.permissions.deniedCommands: Commands the agent may never run — `git push`, `rm`, `kubectl`. Matched anywhere in the command line, so denying `git push` also refuses `npm test && git push`: a refusal that is escaped by typing `&&` protects nobody. Word boundaries are still respected, so denying `rm` does not deny `rmdir`.
config.endpoints.servers: Extra model servers, on this machine or on your network. Each one is probed and its models appear in the picker: `{ "name": "GPU box", "url": "http://192.168.1.50:11434/v1" }`. An address on your own network is treated as local — nothing is billed and nothing is pseudonymised, because nothing leaves.
config.endpoints.servers.name: How the server is named in the picker.
config.endpoints.servers.url: The OpenAI-compatible base URL, ending in /v1.
config.skills.disabled: Skills that are not offered in the `/` list, by name (`/tests`). Toggled from the skills button in the composer. Storing what is OFF rather than what is on means a skill added by an update, or by a colleague committing a file, arrives switched on rather than invisible.
config.privacy.confirmSend: Preview each question before it is sent: how many tokens it will use and what it will cost. Shown as a card in the conversation, never as a dialog. The card's **Always** button sets this to `never`.
command.setLanguage.title: Language of the panel
config.agents.disabled: Sub-agents that may not be dispatched, by name. Toggled from the skills button in the composer, alongside the skills.
config.skills.groups: Which families of skills are in play: `general`, `frontend`, `javascript`, `python`, `java`, `dotnet`, `cpp`, `go`, `rust`, `flutter`, `data`, `devops`, `design`, `security`, `rpg`, `dds`, `db2i`, `cl`. Families are **opt-in** and only `general` is on to begin with, so the `/` list holds what you chose rather than everything that exists. Set from the new-conversation screen or the composer's skills button.

config.ibmi.integration: Whether the IBM i tools and the `+` menu's IBM i entries appear. They need **Code for IBM i**; nothing here works without it.
config.ibmi.integration.auto: Only when Code for IBM i is connected — nothing to see for anyone who does not use it.
config.ibmi.integration.on: Whenever Code for IBM i is installed, connected or not.
config.ibmi.integration.off: Never, even when Code for IBM i is there.
